title: Dedicated pool warmup starvation caused by leader liveness regression
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a traffic spike on 2025-02-18 several customers experienced silent capacity shortfalls in Dedicated reserved pools: warmup tasks that pre-warm GPU slots for tenants were not consistently completing, causing repeated cold starts and elevated latency. This incident surfaced via a NexaHealth escalation (page #358) and internal monitoring alerting on spike in 95th percentile latency and a rapid drop in 'tenant_warmed_slots' metrics. Investigation found a regression in leader liveness handling that caused warmup coordinator leaders to step down early and lose in-flight warmup signals. The consequence was sustained headroom collapse and failure to trigger burst allocations for affected tenants.
root_cause: A small regression in the leader liveness expiration logic (introduced in runtime-1.17.3) reduced the effective grace period for warmup coordinators. When combined with transient GC pauses on the coordinator host and a race in the warmup task state machine, leaders were observed to step down before confirming warmup completion. Stepping down cleared local in-memory warmup state without persisting progress to the global lease, so no other replica assumed the remaining warmup work promptly. This prevented reserved-pool headroom from being restored during bursts.
mitigation: Hotfix rolled to production (dedicated-2025.02.1) that: 1) increases leader liveness grace window for warmup coordinators, 2) makes warmup state durable to the shared raft store before leader transitions, and 3) adds a fallback that re-queues warmup tasks on leader loss. Deployed progressive canary across regions and applied emergency capacity compensation for impacted tenants (temp token-based pre-allocations).
postmortem_action_items: Add unit + integration tests simulating leader preemption during warmup (owner: Rafael)
Instrument new 'warmup_progress_persisted' metric and alert when not updated for >30s (owner: Saira)
Add chaos test in CI to simulate GC pauses and leader restarts during warmup flow (owner: Tomas)
Adjust autoscaler policy to tolerate short warmup regressions by pre-reserving minimal burst tokens for high-SLO tenants (owner: Product)
Run blameless postmortem review with NexaHealth and document SLA mitigation and credits process (owner: Maya)
